_note: Written BEFORE any run of this rule: no price frame of us500 or ger40 had been read (only the parquet schema and row-group timestamp statistics), no order built, nothing simulated. IN SAMPLE ONLY.
frozen_name: FOMC-cycle even/odd weeks, long-short on US500
frozen_rule:
CALENDAR:
- Day 0 = each scheduled FOMC statement day (lab/tracks/seasonality/calendars.py). The 2020 unscheduled actions are ignored.
- t = NYSE trading days relative to day 0.
- Weeks: W0 = t in [-1,+3], W1 = [4,8], W2 = [9,13], W3 = [14,18], W4 = [19,23], W5 = [24,28], W6 = [29,33].
- The five days [-6,-2] before the next day 0 form W-1 and override any later week of the current cycle. Days past 33 are ignored.

POSITION: LONG in W0, W2, W4, W6; SHORT in W1, W3, W5; flat in W-1.

ENTRY: open of the first M1 bar at or after 15:55 NY on the trading day before the week's first day.
EXIT: 15:55 NY on the week's last day. Consecutive weeks exit and re-enter in the same minute.
STOP: disaster stop at 3 x ATR(20) of daily bars, from the fill.

SIZING: 1 R = stop distance.

INSTRUMENT: us500. ger40 runs the same calendar at 15:55 NY on the same days, as a mechanism check.
frozen_test_plan:
10 configurations. The verdict is read on (1) only.

(1) Main on us500, as in 'rule'.

Neighbours:
(2) entry and exit at 15:30 NY
(3) week boundaries shifted by +1 trading day
(4) stop 2 x ATR(20)
(5) stop 4 x ATR(20)
(6) W-1 short instead of flat

Mechanism check: (7) the same calendar on ger40. Its expectancy must be positive (a declared condition, not a pass on its own).

Diagnostic: (8) long-only even weeks, reported against the null; it cannot be selected.

Stress: (9) main at costs x1.5.

Null: (10) calendar rule, so mode 'time': the same trades (side, stop, duration) at fully random moments, 200 replays.

COST: us500 spread 0.54 bp; market slippage 0.2 bp per side; stop 0.5 bp; long-side swap 5.5 %/yr with the Friday triple (about 10.7 bp per long week); shorts pay no swap (credits ignored). About 7 bp a trade on average.

PASS = PROTOCOL_V3 s.4 single-sleeve bars on us500, plus the ger40 condition.

DECLARED NOW: the expected t is about 2.3 even at the full published effect, so a fail is likely even if the effect is real. The result closes the question either way.

Expected n about 400.
frozen_instruments: us500: FP cash CFD, frame lab/data/fp/us500_m1.parquet, 2013-2021. ger40 on the same calendar as a mechanism check.
frozen_why:
P = 0.07 (in sample) x 0.22 (VAL given an in-sample pass) = 1.5 %. Correlation with the account about 0.08, q 0.54.

SUB-SCORES (0-10):
- prior 2
- trades 4: about 45 a year, about 400 in 2013-2021
- independence 7: a weekly clock no sleeve uses, alternating long and short
- cost 6: about 7 bp a trade on average, because long weeks pay about 10.7 bp of swap; needs about 33 bp gross per trade
- simplicity 8
- MQL5/FP 7: the FOMC table is embedded (it is published a year ahead); us500 0.1 lot at a 3 x ATR(20) stop is about 2 % of 1,000 EUR, and 1 % from about 2,000 EUR

NEVER TRIED: no 'cycle', 'even week' or Cieslak in results/, r2/, tracks/ or the protocols. The events track tested windows of minutes to one session around releases (results/r2/events/).

POWER, declared before the run: at the full 1994-2013 size (about 33 bp gross per weekly trade), the net t on about 400 trades with an sd of about 230 bp is about 2.3. It can pass only if the effect is intact or larger. The week-0 part, the pre-FOMC drift, has already shrunk to +6.2 bp (t 0.98, n 70) in the lab's data, against about 49 bp in the literature (results/r2/events/desc3_windows.txt).

The calendar is on disk: lab/tracks/seasonality/calendars.py (FOMC 2013-2026).

configurations.name: diag_long_even
configurations.role: diagnostic, reported against its own random-time null, cannot be selected

readings_of_open_details.D1_in_sample_only: Frames lab/data/fp/us500_m1.parquet and ger40_m1.parquet are read with the parquet row filter ts < 2022-01-01 00:00 UTC (pandas.read_parquet(filters=[('ts','<',CUT)])), max(ts) < CUT is asserted, and these slices are passed explicitly to every function (goldlab.r2.load and goldlab.r2.null_test, which read the whole frame, are NOT used). The official trades of the ten are read with the filter entry_time < 2022-01-01 in the same statement; rows with exit_time >= 2022-01-01 are dropped. The FOMC list is cut at < 2022-01-01 when imported: the 2022-2026 dates are never used (no in-sample day depends on them: the W-1 of 2022-01-26 starts in January 2022). NYSE days are generated by the holiday rule up to 2021-12-31 only.
readings_of_open_details.D2_calendar: Day 0 = the FOMC list of lab/tracks/seasonality/calendars.py (2013-01-30 ... 2021-12-15). FOMC_UNSCHEDULED (2020-03-03, 2020-03-15) is ignored; the cancelled March 2020 meeting is not in the list, so 2020-01-29 -> 2020-04-29 is one cycle (its days past 33 are ignored, as the rule says). NYSE trading days = weekdays that are not full closures of r2/tracks/idx_us/idxus_lib.us_holidays (holidays + 2018-12-05); 13:00 early closes are NYSE trading days and are counted in t.
readings_of_open_details.D3_week_labels: General form with a shift s (s = 0 for every configuration except (3), s = 1). A NYSE day of index i belongs to the cycle of the latest day 0 F with i >= F - 1 + s; t = i - F. With F' the next listed day 0, u = i - F'. W-1 if -6+s <= u <= -2+s (it overrides any week of the current cycle); else W_k if 5k-1+s <= t <= 5k+3+s (k = 0..6); else (t > 33+s) the day is ignored (flat). Days before the first cycle are flat unless they are the W-1 of 2013-01-30. The last in-sample cycle (2021-12-15) has no next day 0 inside the sample, hence no W-1 (none of its days before 2022 could be one). For (3) 'week boundaries shifted by +1 trading day' every boundary moves by +1: W0 = [0,4] ... W6 = [30,34], W-1 = [-5,-1] before the next day 0, days past 34 ignored.
readings_of_open_details.D4_positions_and_trades: The position over NYSE day i (held from 15:55 NY of day i-1 to 15:55 NY of day i) is +1 in W0/W2/W4/W6, -1 in W1/W3/W5, 0 in W-1 and on ignored days ((6): -1 in W-1; (8): 0 in W1/W3/W5). One trade = one maximal run of consecutive NYSE days carrying the same (cycle, week) label and a non-zero position. A week shortened by the W-1 override is traded over its remaining days (literal reading of 'override any later week'; the judge's n of about 400, about 45 a year, counts these). Consecutive weeks are separate trades that exit and re-enter in the same minute, also when the side does not change (only possible in (6): W5 -> W-1), each paying its own round trip.
readings_of_open_details.D5_entry: Market order at the OPEN of the first M1 bar starting at or after 15:55:00 New York (DST-aware) on the NYSE trading day before the week's first day (goldlab.data.entry_index). FP fills: long at the ask, short at the bid, plus 0.2 bp market slippage.
readings_of_open_details.D6_exit: Time exit scheduled at 15:55:00 New York on the week's last day, executed at the OPEN of the first bar at or after that time; if that time falls inside a market closure (next bar more than 30 minutes later: 13:15 ET early closes, holidays, data holes) at the open of the last bar before the closure (goldlab.data.exit_index, the lab's convention). On such days the exit and the next entry are therefore not in the same minute (the next entry follows the literal ENTRY text: first bar at or after 15:55, after the closure); the number of trades concerned is reported. A trade whose entry bar is not before its exit bar is dropped (counted). A trade whose scheduled exit is at or after 2022-01-01 00:00 UTC is not simulated (its exit is outside the sample; at most one per configuration: the W2 trade of the 2021-12-15 cycle), and a block reaching 2021-12-31 before its nominal end is treated the same way.
readings_of_open_details.D7_stop: Disaster stop at k x ATR(20) of daily bars, k = 3 ((4): 2, (5): 4). ATR(20) = the lab's daily ATR for the index CFDs, r2/tracks/idx_us/idxus_lib.daily_atr / atr_at with n = 20: simple 20-day average of the true range of NY 17:00 trading days (mid prices, days with fewer than 600 M1 bars dropped) = MT5 iATR(D1, 20) on FP's server clock, the value the robot would read. The value used for an entry decided at 15:55 NY on day D is that of the last trading day completed (17:00 NY) at or before the decision, i.e. the previous trading day; no trade before 20 true ranges exist. The distance is fixed in price at the decision; stop = fill - side x distance; it is a resting order, filled at its level, or at the bar open if a bar gaps through it, plus 0.5 bp. A stop distance below 3 x (ask - bid) at the open of the entry bar is refused (hard rule 4; counted).
readings_of_open_details.D8_costs_base: FP frames (spread inside the quotes: us500 0.4 pt at 7,377 = 0.54 bp, ger40 1.6 pt at 25,820 = 0.62 bp, Dukascopy intraday shape) and goldlab.r2.costs(sym): market slippage 0.2 bp per side, stop slippage 0.5 bp, swap = rate / 360 x entry price per 17:00 NY rollover crossed, Friday counted three times (goldlab.sim): us500 long 5.5 %/yr (7 nights = 10.7 bp a normal long week), ger40 long 4.1 %/yr, shorts 0 (credits ignored); no commission. Every trade crosses rollovers, so swaps always apply to the long weeks.
readings_of_open_details.D9_stress: (9) 'main at costs x1.5'. The judge's COST paragraph counts spread, slippage AND the long swap as the costs ('about 7 bp a trade'). Most conservative reading: all of them x 1.5: spread x1.5 (goldlab.sim.apply_spread_mult, orders rebuilt on the widened frame), slippage x1.5 (r2.costs(sym, 1.5)) and swap rates x1.5 (the lab's usual stress leaves the swap unchanged; that figure is given as information only, by exact arithmetic on the same stressed trades, and is never used for the verdict).
readings_of_open_details.D10_null: (10) mode 'time' (calendar rule): 200 replays, numpy default_rng(0). Each filled trade of the main (FP costs) is re-entered at market at the open of a uniformly drawn M1 bar of the in-sample slice, with its side, its stop distance as a fraction of price (risk / entry x mid close of the drawn bar, as r2.null_test), its scheduled time-exit delay in M1 bars (exit_i - fill_i, as r2.null_test), no target. Only difference with r2.null_test: draws are limited so that the whole replay lies inside the slice (bar index <= N - 1 - delay), since a replay may not run into 2022. FP costs, swaps included; every replay trade taken (no_overlap = False, as the main). Statistic: mean R per trade. Percentile = share of the 200 replay means strictly below the main's mean R; pass if >= 97.5.
readings_of_open_details.D11_ger40: (7) the same day labels (NYSE days, US FOMC days), entry and exit at 15:55 NY on the same days, on lab/data/fp/ger40_m1.parquet (it starts 2013-09-30, so the check covers late 2013 to 2021), ATR(20) of ger40's own daily bars, r2.costs('ger40'). Days on which ger40 has no bar at 15:55 NY follow D5 / D6 mechanically. Declared condition: mean R (FP costs) > 0.
readings_of_open_details.D12_diagnostic_8: (8) long in W0/W2/W4/W6, flat in W1/W3/W5 and W-1, FP costs. 'Reported against the null': its own random-time null (D10's procedure on its own trades, 200 replays, seed 0) is reported with it. It cannot be selected and judges nothing.
readings_of_open_details.D13_criteria: Read on (1) only, PROTOCOL_V3 s.4 single-sleeve bars: n >= 250; PF >= 1.12 on R; t >= 2.5 (mean R / (sd R, ddof 1) x sqrt(n)); >= 60 % of calendar years positive (sum of R by entry year; 2013-2021 = 9 years, so at least 6); PF of (9) >= 1.04; median PF of the five neighbours (2)-(6) >= 1.06; every-signal expectancy > 0 (a calendar rule: every week is a signal, the main takes all of them and they never overlap, so it equals the main's expectancy; simulated with no_overlap = False); hold <= 5 trading days, counted in NYSE trading days (the protocol's own unit; the lab's 192-hour proxy is reported too, since a five-trading-day week that spans holidays lasts up to 11 calendar days); null percentile >= 97.5. Plus the judge's condition: expectancy of (7) > 0. PASS only if all hold.
readings_of_open_details.D14_reported_not_judged: For each configuration: the lab's report fields (n, PF, t, expectancy, total R, by year, long/short, weeks), net bp per trade, swap bp per trade, results by week label (W-1, W0..W6). For the main only: gross bp per trade (an accounting re-run of the same orders on mid quotes with zero cost, as r2.evaluate's 'gross'). Weekly correlation of the main with the sum of the ten and with each of the three clusters, 2014-2021: weekly sums of R by exit week (W-SUN, UTC), every calendar week counted, Pearson; the ten and the clusters as in the other round-4 tracks (us100: ocm4 + noise30; gold: donch4h_stop + orb_asia_2d_buf10 + GOLD_FRI_PM; crypto: brk72_24h_wd btc/eth + F1_brk_ridge_filter btc/eth + nq_btc_follow).
readings_of_open_details.D15_causality: Truncation test on at least 50 decisions: 60 trades of the main drawn with numpy default_rng(1) plus the first and the last trade. (a) Decisions rebuilt on the frame cut just before the decision instant (rows ts < 15:55 NY of the entry day) must give the same side, the same decision and exit times and the same stop distance (exact). (b) Each trade re-simulated alone on the frame cut just after its exit bar (rows ts <= exit bar) must give the same exit time, exit price, reason and R. Stops are resting orders; the time exit is a clock decision known at the close of the 15:54 bar and executed at the open of the 15:55 bar.
readings_of_open_details.D16_trials: Ten lines in results/r2/round4/fomc_cycle/trials.jsonl, one per declared configuration, written whatever the result. Nothing else is simulated except the accounting gross re-run of the main, the null replays of (10) and (8), and the causality test.

criteria.years_pos>=60%: years of (1) with sum R > 0, at least 6 of 9
